Secondary 7th Chords · Level 1.heading: Hear a different seventh chord. Choose its type.
Secondary 7th Chords · Level 1.intro: You will hear four notes played together. Choose the chord type that matches the sound.

steps.title: Listen to the chord
steps.description: Press Play to hear all four notes together. Listen to the sound they make as a group. You can listen again whenever you need to.

steps.title: Choose the chord type
steps.description: Choose the chord name that matches what you hear. The answer buttons show the six chord types used in this lesson.

steps.title: Submit your answer
steps.description: When you are ready, press Submit Answer. You can change your choice before you submit.

Secondary 7th Chords · Level 1.about: These are four-note chords with different combinations of chord notes. For example, Minor-Major 7th combines a minor three-note chord with a major seventh: F, A♭, C and E. In the chord names, ♭5 means the fifth is lowered by one small keyboard step, and ♯5 means it is raised by one small keyboard step. This lesson uses chords built on F. The notes use a close layout. Choose the chord type only; there is no separate inversion answer.
Secondary 7th Chords · Level 1.layoutCaption: F minor-major seventh: F, A♭ and C, with E added.
Secondary 7th Chords · Level 1.exampleExplanation: This visual example is F minor-major seventh. Choose Minor-Major 7th. During the quiz, choose the type of chord you hear.
